media_work.title: Strengthening Forensic Science in the United States: A Path Forward
media_work.creator_name: Committee on Identifying the Needs of the Forensic Science Community, National Research Council
media_work.focus_or_theme: Comprehensive assessment of the state of forensic science in the United States and recommendations for improvement to reduce wrongful convictions
media_work.key_statistics: The report notes that forensic science analyses may have contributed to wrongful convictions of innocent people

key_quotes_raw: The benefits of improving and regulating the forensic science disciplines are clear: assisting law enforcement officials, enhancing homeland security, and reducing the risk of wrongful conviction.

Further improvements in forensic science practices should reduce the occurrence of wrongful convictions, which reduces the risk that true offenders continue to commit crimes while innocent persons inappropriately serve time.

Forensic science analyses may have contributed to wrongful convictions of innocent people. This fact has demonstrated the potential danger of giving undue weight to evidence and testimony derived from imperfect testing and analysis.
systemic_issues_raw: Fragmentation of the forensic science system across federal, state, and local jurisdictions
Lack of mandatory standardization, certification, and accreditation
Absence of rigorous, mandatory certification programs for forensic scientists
Insufficient research to validate many forensic science methods
Inadequate education and training for forensic scientists
Lack of peer-reviewed, published studies establishing the scientific bases and reliability of many forensic methods
Insufficient resources for public forensic science laboratories
Potential bias and conflicts of interest when forensic laboratories are administratively part of law enforcement agencies
policy_recommendations_raw: Creation of a new, independent federal entity—the National Institute of Forensic Science (NIFS)—to oversee and regulate the field
Establishment of standard terminology and reporting practices
Implementation of mandatory certification for forensic science professionals
Mandatory accreditation for forensic science laboratories
Removal of public forensic laboratories from administrative control of law enforcement agencies
Increased research to establish the scientific bases and validity of forensic methods
Improved education and training for forensic scientists
Development of tools for advancing measurement, validation, reliability, and proficiency testing in forensic science
Improved practices and standards for analyzing and reporting on evidence
Improved medical examiner and coroner systems
additional_resources_raw: The report was the result of a comprehensive study conducted over two years
The committee heard testimony from numerous experts in the field
The report includes detailed analyses of various forensic science disciplines
The report has been cited extensively in subsequent research and policy discussions
media_item.item_title: Book Content: Strengthening Forensic Science in the United States: A Path Forward
media_item.focus_or_theme: Comprehensive assessment of the state of forensic science in the United States and recommendations for improvement to reduce wrongful convictions
media_item.summary_notes: This report represents a landmark assessment of forensic science in the United States. It takes a comprehensive, systemic approach to examining the entire field of forensic science and its role in the justice system.  The report acknowledges that flawed forensic science has contributed to wrongful convictions and argues that improving forensic science practices is essential for reducing such miscarriages of justice.  The report's recommendations aim to create a more reliable, scientifically sound forensic science system.
media_item.case_details_raw: Unlike the previous books researched, this report does not focus on specific named cases of wrongfully convicted individuals. Instead, it takes a systemic approach, examining the forensic science disciplines as a whole and how their shortcomings can contribute to wrongful convictions. The report references studies and analyses of wrongful convictions in the United States but does not detail specific cases.

research_notes_raw: This report was commissioned by Congress in 2005 and published in 2009. It has had a significant impact on discussions about forensic science reform and has been cited by organizations like The Innocence Project as a foundational document for understanding the relationship between forensic science and wrongful convictions.
